title: Execution-Trace Guided Remasking for Diffusion Code Generation

contributions.purpose: Give diffusion code models semantic guidance about where errors occur instead of confidence-based remasking heuristics.
contributions.mechanism: Execution-trace guided remasking pipeline: parse exception tracebacks or line-level execution traces from failing unit tests, map failure-relevant lines to token indices, and remask only those tokens for conditional diffusion repair.
contributions.evaluation: Implemented as a three-stage inference-time algorithm (initial generation, execution-based localization, targeted conditional repair) evaluated on MBPP+.
contributions.source_quote: We introduce an execution-trace guided remasking pipeline that uses runtime diagnostics (exception tracebacks, line-level traces) to localize failures and target repair in diffusion code generation.

contributions.purpose: Quantify the accuracy gain from trace-guided repair over no-repair and confidence-based remasking baselines.
contributions.mechanism: Pass@1 comparison on MBPP+ against the no-repair baseline and CORE with statistical significance testing.
contributions.evaluation: 31.22% pass@1 on MBPP+, +11.38pp over the no-repair baseline and +4.24 points over CORE (p < 0.001).
contributions.source_quote: On MBPP+, our method achieves 31.22% pass@1, an 11.38 percentage point improvement over the no-repair baseline and 4.24 points over CORE, with statistical significance (p < 0.001).

contributions.purpose: Explain why semantic localization is essential for effective diffusion repair.
contributions.mechanism: Edit-distance analysis comparing code modifications made by trace-guided repair versus global low-confidence repair.
contributions.evaluation: Trace-guided repair makes meaningful modifications (mean edit distance 10.01 tokens) while global low-confidence repair rarely changes code (89.4% zero-edit fraction).
contributions.source_quote: We provide analysis showing that trace-guided repair produces meaningful code modifications (mean edit distance 10.01 tokens) while global low-confidence repair rarely changes code (89.4% zero-edit fraction), explaining why semantic localization is essential for effective repair.

self_declared_provenance.quote: This approach bridges the gap between diffusion-based generation and execution-guided debugging.
Our work builds on these foundations but focuses on post-generation repair rather than generation-time constraints.

However, these methods select tokens to remask based on model confidence or heuristics, without semantic guidance about where errors actually occur. Our approach addresses this limitation by using execution feedback to localize failures.
Our work brings execution guidance to diffusion models, leveraging their native remasking capability for targeted repair rather than full regeneration.
